headline: Iris Ohyama Cloud Breach May Expose 7.7M
standfirst: A third-party cloud breach at Iris Ohyama may have exposed 7.7 million people's data; Brava Security launched with $15 million for AI attack telemetry.
bodyMarkdown:
## Breaches

Iris Ohyama says unauthorized third-party cloud access may have exposed data on about 7.7 million people [[s1]]. Access details were not supplied.

## Industry

Brava Security emerged from stealth with $15 million for a multi-agent AI platform that generates telemetry an attack would produce to fix enterprise defense gaps [[s2]]. Analysis: investor interest in proactive AI defense continues; efficacy is unproven.

selected.title: Iris Ohyama data cloud breach exposes info of 7.7 million customers
selected.excerpt: Japanese manufacturer Iris Ohyama, the operator of the Iris Plaza shopping platform, disclosed that personal information belonging to about 7.7 million people may have been exposed after unauthorized access to a third-party cloud service the company used. [...]
selected.angle: A third-party cloud compromise exposed data on 7.7 million Iris Ohyama customers, underscoring cloud supply-chain and data governance risk.

selected.title: Brava Security Emerges From Stealth With $15 Million in Funding
selected.excerpt: Its multi-agent AI platform generates the telemetry an attack would produce to fix gaps in enterprise defenses. The post Brava Security Emerges From Stealth With $15 Million in Funding appeared first on SecurityWeek.
selected.angle: Brava Security's $15M launch signals continued investor interest in AI-driven proactive enterprise defense and attack telemetry.
